overview.heading: What is a Bachelor of Occupational Therapy?
paragraphs: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy is an undergraduate health course that trains students to help people regain everyday skills after illness, injury, disability, or developmental conditions. In India, it is usually a 4 to 4.5 year programme with classroom study, practical work, and clinical training, and most colleges ask for Class 12 Science with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology.

Students learn how to assess a person's movement, memory, hand function, self-care, school tasks, and work routines, then plan activities and exercises that make daily life easier. The work is practical and people-focused, so students spend time in labs, hospital wards, rehabilitation settings, and field placements rather than only studying theory.

After graduation, most people work with hospitals, rehabilitation centres, clinics, special schools, elderly-care services, or community health teams. Because entry requirements can change by institution and the field is health-care based, families should check the current admission rules and the steps needed for local practice or registration before choosing the course.

snapshot.data_note: Pay changes with the type of employer, city, experience, and the patient group served. Private hospitals, rehabilitation centres, teaching roles, and specialist practice can pay differently, so one figure cannot describe every graduate.

salary.note: Typical earnings for occupational therapists in India are around INR 3.9 lakh a year, with reported ranges from about INR 0.3 lakh to INR 8 lakh a year. Early-career pay is usually lower, while experience and specialist roles can raise income.

caution.heading: Be careful if you expect this course to be mostly hospital medicine
points: The work is about helping people function in daily life, not about diagnosing disease or prescribing medicine.
The course needs steady practical effort; students who dislike labs, observation, and supervised clinical work may find it difficult.
Pay can start modestly in some settings, so it suits students who are motivated by care work and long-term growth rather than quick earnings
Admission requirements vary by college, and some institutions expect specific Science subjects and marks at Class 12.

parent_corner.intro: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy suits students who are patient, observant, and comfortable working closely with people. The course is not only about classroom biology; it also includes hands-on practice, communication, and learning how to support recovery and independence. Families should check three things early: whether the college is recognised, whether it includes supervised clinical training, and whether the graduate can register for practice in the state or region where they plan to work. It also helps to ask about hospital postings, internship length, and whether the campus has access to rehabilitation facilities. For students, this course works best when they genuinely enjoy service-oriented work and can handle steady study plus practical training.
